title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to the 1986 'third version' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck's late attempt to axiomatise 'tame topology' (the programme announced in the Esquisse d'un programme, 1984). The setting is the following.
- M is a set of elementary pieces ('modèles', or strata-like cells), ordered by ≤.
- \U0001D4D5 is the set of 'lieux' (closed, locally closed or constructible subsets). Each lieu F has a set F̃ of pieces lying in it.
- X' ≪ X is a 'neighbourhood-like' relation: X' is a small tube or germ-neighbourhood of X, or lies in the star of X. The next page explicitly calls G' ≪ G a 'voisinage' of G.
- Disjointness was defined on p.7: X ∥ Y iff X and Y are ≤-incomparable and have no common minorant. For lieux, F ∥ G iff F, G are incomparable and F∩G = ∅_\U0001D4D5, equivalently iff the pieces of F are pairwise disjoint from the pieces of G.
- F'_L denotes the 'trace' or germ of F' along L. Page 9 defines X'_L ∥ Y'_L to mean: every X'' ≤ X' and Y'' ≤ Y' with X'' ≪ L and Y'' ≪ L are disjoint.

The page is about compatibility axioms between disjointness and neighbourhoods for an 'atelier'.

First crossed-out version (At DC 1, 'axiome des ateliers spéciaux'). Let X, Y ∈ M, L = X∩Y, X' ≪ X and Y' ≪ Y, with X' ∥ L and Y' ∥ L. Then X' ∥ Y'.
- Cor 1 (crossed out): F ∥ G, F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G ⇒ F' ∥ G'. Disjoint lieux have disjoint (small) neighbourhoods.
- Cor 2 (crossed out): the relative version with L = F∩G.
- A second attempt, At DC 2 (also crossed out), states the converse 'criterion' of the previous page: if all such X', Y' are disjoint, then X and Y are incomparable.

Top-left margin: a proof that under these hypotheses X'∩Y' = ∅ is automatic. Suppose Z ≤ X' and Z ≤ Y'. Then Z ≪ X and Z ≪ Y, so Z ≪ X∩Y = L. But Z ≤ X' ∥ L, a contradiction. Hence only incomparability of X' and Y' is really at stake.

The retained statement, 'Propriété 1'. Let F, G ∈ \U0001D4D5 be non-disjoint (written as a crossed relation), L = F∩G, F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G. Then F' and G' meet iff their germs along L meet: F' ∥ G' ⇔ F'_L ∥ G'_L. Informally, two small tubes around F and G can only meet near the common part L. This is a 'localisation of intersections to the intersection locus', i.e. a tubular-neighbourhood separation property.

Grothendieck says this is equivalent to a criterion, renamed from the old 'At 12', now 'At DD1':
- Hypotheses: X, Y, X', Y' ∈ M, X and Y incomparable, X' ≪ X, Y' ≪ Y, K = X∩Y = sup of common minorants.
- Conclusion: X'_L ∥ Y'_L implies X' ∥ Y'.
- He notes the converse is (always) true.
- Corollaries: Cor 1 is Property 1. Cor 2 says F ∥ G ⇒ small neighbourhoods are disjoint, and in general F' ∥ G' ⇔ F'_L ∥ G'_L.

Bottom-left margin, with a small figure: 'Critère de compatibilité … faux dans le cas linéaire!' There is an example where X'_L ∥ Y'_L but X' and Y' are not disjoint, contradicting At 11 (cf. 'GF 68'). This prompts, on page 9, a weakened 'Propriété 1'_0' and 'Ax CD 1'_0'. There the implication ⇒ is always valid and only ⇐ is axiomatised; Ax CD is then regarded as 'obligatoire'.

Purpose: to isolate the minimal poset-theoretic axioms that make neighbourhoods behave as in genuine tame (stratified, semialgebraic or PL) spaces. These are separation of disjoint lieux by neighbourhoods, and localisation of intersections of tubes along the intersection.
errors: The page is visibly a working draft. At DC 1 and At DC 2 are struck out, and the hypothesis on X' in At DC 1 ('X' ∥ Z pour Z ∈ X, Y') is garbled.

Grothendieck himself records (bottom-left margin) that the compatibility criterion is false in the 'linear' case. He gives an example with X'_L ∥ Y'_L but X', Y' not disjoint. Property 1 / At DD1 as stated therefore cannot be a general axiom, which is why it is weakened on p.9.
In At DD1 the intersection is first called K and then L is used in the conclusion; notation is inconsistent (K vs L).

The symbol used in Property 1 and At DD1 oscillates between 'incomparable' (crossed ≶) and 'not disjoint'. As written ('Alors F' ≶ G' ⇔ F'_L ≶ G'_L') the statement is ambiguous. Page 9 makes clear the intended content is about disjointness ∥.

ideas.what: Axiomatic notion of 'atelier': a poset of pieces with lieux and a neighbourhood relation ≪, used to found tame topology combinatorially
ideas.modern_name: axiomatic tame topology; compare o-minimal structures and abstract stratified spaces / posets of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); stratified-space axiomatics: Whitney, Thom, Mather
ideas.where_published: Only the programme (not the axiomatics) appears in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (1984)

ideas.what: Separation: disjoint lieux have disjoint small neighbourhoods (F ∥ G, F' ≪ F, G' ≪ G ⇒ F' ∥ G')
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Urysohn normality; regular neighbourhoods in PL topology: Whitehead, Cohen)

ideas.what: Localisation: small neighbourhoods of F and G meet iff their germs along L = F∩G meet (Propriété 1 / At DD1), with an explicit counterexample in the 'linear' case leading to a weakened one-directional axiom
ideas.modern_name: localisation of intersections of tubular neighbourhoods to the intersection locus (germ-level transversality-type property)
ideas.usually_credited_to: no single source; implicit in regular-neighbourhood theory and o-minimal tubular neighbourhood results

ideas.what: Disjointness defined purely order-theoretically (incomparable and no common minorant)
ideas.modern_name: disjointness in a poset / meet-semilattice (no common lower bound)

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to axiomatise, purely in terms of an order ≤ and a neighbourhood relation ≪ on 'pieces', the property that tubes around F and G intersect only along the germ at F∩G. He finds that the two-sided version fails in the 'linear' model and retreats to a one-directional axiom (p.9). A precise poset/locale-style axiomatics of neighbourhood germs for tame spaces of this kind does not seem to have been developed in the literature, which went the o-minimal or stratified-∞-category route instead.
missed.quote: Alors F' ≶ G' ⇔ F'_L ≶ G'_L ... Critère de compatibilité ... faux dans le cas linéaire !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could inform purely combinatorial or point-free foundations of tame or stratified topology, e.g. comparing with o-minimal regular neighbourhoods or exit-path/stratified-space frameworks. The impact is modest and speculative.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting unpublished glimpse of Grothendieck's 1986 axiomatics for tame topology ('ateliers', disjointness/neighbourhood compatibility), including a self-found counterexample. The individual statements are, however, natural separation/tubular-neighbourhood properties. They are not deep new theorems, and the framework is draft-level and partly crossed out.
transcription_corrections: In Property 1 and At DD1, the relation symbol written is a crossed ≶ ('incomparable' / non-disjoint in the draft's usage), not ∦. The transcription renders several crossed ≶ as ∦ (e.g. 'X ≶ Y', 'F ≶ G').
In At DD1, 'Soient X, Y ∈ X', Y'' should read 'Soient X, Y et X', Y' ∈ M' (with 'ancien' inserted above). The intersection is denoted K, while the conclusion uses L.
'Ceci est équivalent [?] Critère [?] At 12' is better read as 'Ceci est équivalent au Critère ... At 12, qui prend le nom de l'ancien' (i.e. renamed At DD1).
The first line ends roughly 'bien qu'elle soit conséquence des diverses façons de démontrer' (illegible); 'serve' is likely 'soit'.
